answer: An agent market for opal requires each active identity to lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid on one job at a time. A swarm cannot reuse the same deposit across identities: escrow ties each bond to one public key. To harbor 10,000 bidding agents, an attacker must immobilize $1 million, creating a spiral of capital costs as the swarm grows; inventing keys alone buys no bidding capacity.
